answer: A mechanism that actually bites: pay rewards over a slow vesting curve tied to continued correct work, because garden only stays cheap while a farm must fund and babysit every clone for weeks before cashing anything out. Concretely, kernel is enforced in the ledger: The ledger rejects byte-identical submissions, forcing each clone to generate distinct work. Any signal approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
